key_insight: DropKV turns KV-cache eviction into a decoupled per-token scoring problem, making near-optimal cache reduction both theoretically tractable and practical for long-context LLMs.
engineering_relevance: It offers a kernel-friendly eviction strategy that lowers memory pressure and speeds up prefill without requiring full attention-matrix materialization.
method: Decouple residual-output perturbation into independent token scores instead of solving a combinatorial eviction problem.
Use a provable constant-factor approximation under an empirically verified cone condition.
Implement fused Triton kernels for efficient scoring and cache eviction.
evidence_signal: On three long-context LLMs, DropKV showed a 19.8x scoring-kernel speedup and up to 9.9% end-to-end prefill speedup, and it outperformed state-of-the-art eviction baselines on RULER and LongBench.
watch_item: The approximation guarantee depends on a cone condition that is empirically verified, so performance may vary if that assumption weakens in other models or workloads.
paper_title: DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction
